intro_5.t: And when I reach the top?

d1.t: Lantern Wharf. Mother started here. So do I.

d2.t: Rainmarket. Everyone here sells something. Tonight, they pay.

d3.t: The Old Quarter. Old families. Old grudges. Older debts.

d4.t: Velvet Row. Pretty lights hide the ugliest ledgers.

d5.t: The Ironworks. Nobody here bends easily. Neither do I.

d6.t: Jade Terrace. A festival night. People are generous when they are happy.

d8.t: The Glass Exchange. Here, the debts have lawyers.

d9.t: Skybridge Heights. I can see her tower from here.

d10.t: The Spire. One more night, Madame Hale.

greet_1.t: Good evening. You know why I am here.

greet_2.t: Evening. The Lantern Bank sends its regards.

greet_3.t: Close the till. We need to talk.

charm_1.t: You have such a lovely shop. It would be a shame to lose it.

charm_2.t: I like you. Let us make this easy for both of us.

charm_3.t: Come now. You are better than a late payment.

press_1.t: The bank is out of patience. So am I.

press_2.t: Tomorrow, someone less polite comes through that door.

press_3.t: Pay tonight, or your name goes up on the Lantern board.

reason_1.t: Look at the numbers. The interest grows every night you wait.

reason_2.t: You signed the contract. I only read it back to you.

reason_3.t: A little now costs less than everything later.

leverage_1.t: I heard something interesting about you today.

leverage_3.t: I know your secret. Let us keep it between us.

offer_1.t: I can shave a little off the top. Tonight only.

offer_2.t: Pay part of it now, and I will forget the late fee.

read_2.t: Tell me what you are really afraid of.

out_1.t: Fine. I know where to find you.

leave_1.t: Think about it. I will be back.

fin_2.t: I brought your money. And your ledger.

end_grace_1.t: I burned the ledger at dawn. Every name in it. Every debt.

end_grace_2.t: The city woke up owing nothing. For one morning, neither did I.

end_fear_1.t: Madame Hale left the tower before sunrise.

end_fear_2.t: Now every light in Lanternport is borrowed from me.

end_fail_1.t: The sun came up, and my ledger was still short.

intro_1.t: In Lanternport, every light is borrowed.

intro_2.t: Your mother collected for me for twenty years. She died owing me one hundred thousand marks.

intro_3.t: Debts do not die, Miss Vale. They are inherited.

intro_4.t: Ten districts. Ten nights. Collect what the city owes me, and climb to my tower before the last dawn.

intro_6.t: Then we will settle your ledger. Face to face.

hale_win_1.t: Adequate. The next district will not be so kind.

hale_win_2.t: You are climbing, Miss Vale. Mind the height.

hale_win_3.t: Your mother would have been faster. But not by much.

hale_fear.t: They whisper your name now. Fear is a fine currency.

hale_fail.t: Dawn, and your ledger is short. Again, Miss Vale.

fin_1.t: So. The daughter reaches the top.

fin_3.t: Then let us settle. Everything has a price.

hale_duel_1.t: You think you can bargain with me?

hale_duel_2.t: I taught your mother everything she knew.

hale_duel_3.t: Careful. I own every door in this city.

oldman_refuse_1.t: I have nothing for you. Get out of my shop.

oldman_refuse_2.t: Your mother at least had manners.

oldman_plead_1.t: Please. The winter was hard on all of us.

oldman_plead_2.t: I have worked this counter for forty years.

oldman_angry_1.t: You threaten me? In my own shop?

oldman_bargain_1.t: Half. I can give you half. No more.

oldman_pay_1.t: Take it. Take it and go.

youngman_refuse_1.t: I, uh, I do not have it right now.

youngman_refuse_2.t: Can we do this next week?

youngman_refuse_3.t: There must be a mistake in the ledger.

youngman_plead_1.t: Please, I have a family. Just a little more time.

youngman_plead_2.t: I am trying, I swear I am trying.

youngman_angry_1.t: You cannot talk to me like that!

youngman_angry_2.t: Get out before I call someone!

youngman_bargain_1.t: What if I pay some now, and the rest later?

youngman_pay_1.t: Okay. Okay. Here. All of it.

youngman_pay_2.t: Just, please, do not come back.

woman_refuse_1.t: Ha! You will get nothing from me, sweetheart.

woman_refuse_2.t: I already paid the last collector.

woman_refuse_3.t: Do I look like a bank to you?

woman_plead_1.t: Business is slow. You can see that yourself.

woman_plead_2.t: Give me one good week. One.

woman_bargain_1.t: I will give you a third tonight. Take it or leave it.

woman_pay_1.t: You have nerve. I will give you that.

oldwoman_refuse_1.t: Oh, my dear. I am just an old woman.

oldwoman_refuse_2.t: My late husband handled the money.

oldwoman_refuse_3.t: Tea? No? Then no money either.

oldwoman_plead_1.t: These flowers are all I have left.

oldwoman_angry_1.t: Your mother would be ashamed of you.

oldwoman_angry_2.t: I will not be spoken to that way.

oldwoman_bargain_1.t: I could spare a little. For you, dear.

oldwoman_pay_1.t: You remind me of her, you know.

oldwoman_pay_2.t: Take it. And be careful out there.
